resources.string: unscroll

Closes the Reels and Shorts screens of Instagram and YouTube by pressing Back. It only receives events from those two apps, reads element ids and labels to recognize those screens, and never stores or sends anything. Turn it off here at any time.
Hidden by unscroll
This is a Reels or Shorts screen.
Go back
Before you turn unscroll on
unscroll closes Reels and Shorts. To do that it uses Android\'s accessibility service. This is exactly what that means:
It only receives events from Instagram and YouTube. Every other app is invisible to it.
In those two apps it reads the structure of the screen (element ids and labels) to tell whether a Reels or Shorts screen is showing.
It acts only by pressing Back or Home, or by covering the screen with a \"Hidden by unscroll\" view.
It never stores, logs or sends what it reads. There is no account, no analytics and no tracking.
You can turn it off at any time, from this app or from your phone\'s accessibility settings.
I understand
Turn unscroll on
Open the accessibility settings, find unscroll under installed or downloaded apps, and switch it on.
Open accessibility settings
If the switch is greyed out

Android blocks accessibility for apps installed outside a store until you allow it.

1. Open the app info screen below.
2. Tap the three-dot menu in the top right corner. It only appears after you tried to switch unscroll on once.
3. Choose "Allow restricted settings".
4. Come back and switch unscroll on.
Open app info
unscroll is on
